role: Critique only; did not implement candidates; did not inspect implementation or parent technical explanations.
method: Inspected all twelve images directly using view_image: three supplied concepts, three original hero baselines, and six r5 hero/inspection captures.
approvalContext: Original large layouts were approved for development, not final biome approval. This review supplies agent judgments only.
comparisonCaveat: Current and original hero framing/sky differ visibly, especially in the wet biomes. These are useful qualitative environment comparisons, not a controlled same-camera material A/B; no topology-change inference is made.

visibleImprovements: Sand now has subtle grain and broad color variation instead of a uniform orange plane.
Rocks have visible mottling and fracture-like marks, with scattered small stones adding scale cues.
desert.readsAsDevelopingEnvironment: Partially: recognizable desert terrain with useful material development, but the hero remains dominated by an almost empty foreground.

highestImpactGaps.visibleEvidence: Hero foreground is a broad nearly featureless sand sheet; scattered dark flecks are too small to read as vegetation. The concept has legible dry grass, shrubs and succulents concentrated around rock groups.
highestImpactGaps.causeHypothesis: Vegetation silhouettes and clustered medium-scale detail may be too sparse or small for this camera.

highestImpactGaps.visibleEvidence: Large hero rocks retain broad angular faces and shallow surface marks. Concept rocks show varied rounded masses, broken edges and crevice shadow; current inspection rocks are consistently faceted.
highestImpactGaps.causeHypothesis: Surface color detail alone may be unable to overcome the simple rock silhouette and face structure.

highestImpactGaps.visibleEvidence: Inspection view exposes large pale/tan ground patches with soft generalized boundaries, whereas the concept's substrate detail is smaller and tied to stones, runoff and plant bases.
highestImpactGaps.causeHypothesis: Broad substrate variation may need more local association with visible features.

desert.mostUsefulNextCorrection: Add one restrained, readable dry vegetation construction in irregular clusters at existing rock bases and foreground edges; preserve the central open sand and existing topology.
desert.decision: Retain material improvement as development progress; do not treat this as final visual approval.

visibleImprovements: Hero now contains a substantial clearly reflective water opening instead of a thin partly obscured water strip.
Foreground soil has mottled tonal detail and nearby plant silhouettes; roots and tree reflections make the wetland identity legible.
mangrove.readsAsDevelopingEnvironment: Yes: it now reads as a developing mangrove environment, though still sparse and visibly procedural.

highestImpactGaps.visibleEvidence: Hero soil-water boundary is visually clean and abrupt, with a broad bare brown foreground. Concept has damp irregular shore texture, root debris, small pools and vegetation transitioning into water.
highestImpactGaps.causeHypothesis: Missing shoreline-scale material and vegetation transitions may make existing banks read as cutouts.

highestImpactGaps.visibleEvidence: Far-bank trees remain separate round crowns with substantial sky gaps; foreground roots are thin repeated lines. The concept has interlocking dark canopy masses and thick tangled root bases.
highestImpactGaps.causeHypothesis: Crown/root silhouette scale and local grouping may be insufficient to create a dense mangrove enclosure.

highestImpactGaps.visibleEvidence: Water reads as a smooth bright mirror, with small regular bands visible in the inspection capture. The concept contains broken reflections, shallow muddy margins and scattered surface interruptions.
highestImpactGaps.causeHypothesis: Reflection breakup and near-shore depth/contact cues may be too weak or too regular.

mangrove.mostUsefulNextCorrection: Develop a narrow damp shoreline band with irregular small plant/root debris clusters and broken shallow reflections along existing water edges, without moving the banks.
mangrove.decision: Retain the more visible water and soil detail. Environment development is clear; substantial reference gaps remain.

visibleImprovements: Hero now clearly displays reflective water between grassy land masses; the baseline read mostly as dry flat ground.
Large foreground grass clusters frame an open approach, and ground variation gives more material identity than the flat baseline.
flooded.readsAsDevelopingEnvironment: Yes: the flooded-grassland identity is now apparent in both hero and inspection views.

highestImpactGaps.visibleEvidence: Foreground grasses form chunky, flat-looking angular blades in similar olive tones. The concept has finer curved overlapping leaves, luminous tips and darker self-shadowed bases.
highestImpactGaps.causeHypothesis: Blade silhouette, curvature and within-clump shading may be limiting detail more than density.

highestImpactGaps.visibleEvidence: Inspection view reveals extensive mostly bare green islands with sparse small plant dots; concept water channels weave through dense grassy hummocks. Hero foreground also has a large smooth dark patch.
highestImpactGaps.causeHypothesis: Vegetation may lack coherent mid-scale patches and damp substrate transitions across the existing islands.

highestImpactGaps.visibleEvidence: Water has very clean bank outlines and broad mirror reflections, with repetitive bands in inspection. Concept water is interrupted by reeds, small ripples and shallow muddy contact zones.
highestImpactGaps.causeHypothesis: Near-water vegetation and irregular reflection/contact breakup may be insufficient.

flooded.mostUsefulNextCorrection: Improve one curved grass-clump representation and use it in irregular groups along existing island margins, with smaller interstitial tufts and darker damp bases; preserve open water and topology.
flooded.decision: Retain the water visibility and stronger foreground framing; develop vegetation representation before declaring this visually convincing.

overall: All three candidates visibly improve on their structural baselines. Wet-biome water visibility is a meaningful improvement. None approaches the supplied concepts closely enough for final visual approval; material marks currently outpace coherent vegetation and shoreline detail. No structural rebuild is recommended from this review.
